forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Broxtowe's 2025/26 General Fund underspent by £2.5m, leaving a £5.7m reserve at 31 March 2026
news_drafts.lead:
Broxtowe Borough Council underspent its General Fund revenue budget by £2.5m in 2025/26. That left a General Fund Reserve of £5.7m at 31 March 2026, according to the council's Medium Term Financial Strategy and Business Strategy, dated October 2026, which goes to Cabinet on 3 November.

The paper attributes the underspend to a mix of underspends, additional income, budget carry forwards, changes in provisions, government grants and financial management. It does not give a figure for each of these.

The 2025/26 outturn is the starting point for the reserve forecasts in the strategy. The £5.7m balance is the figure from which the council's projections for later years begin.
news_drafts.paper_title: MTFS and Business Strategy Oct-26 FINAL

news_drafts.headline: Broxtowe housing scheme delivered a year early as council addresses regulator concerns
news_drafts.lead: Broxtowe's Hemlock Gate housing scheme is completing in 2026/27, a year ahead of schedule, allowing the council to bring forward £1.838m in spending and start collecting rental income for its housing account sooner than expected. The acceleration comes as the developer prioritises the council's social housing units during a slowdown in the housing market. Meanwhile, the council is responding to a C3 judgment from the Regulator of Social Housing following an October inspection by implementing a refreshed improvement plan and restructuring its housing teams to centralise compliance, with changes to take effect in October 2026. The council is also managing immediate pressures on its capital programme, including an additional £120,000 of borrowing needed to upgrade lifeline alarm systems in its Independent Living schemes before the analogue phone line switch-off on 31 January 2027, and a 53 per cent cost increase in council office repairs due to scaffolding price inflation. The section 151 officer, the council's chief finance officer, has flagged potential future cost pressures on the housing account, though none have materialised yet.

findings.paper_title: MTFS and Business Strategy Oct-26 FINAL
findings.headline: The MTFS does not take account of the impact of Local Government Reorganisation.
findings.detail: The paper says the projected end date of the strategy may extend beyond the potential start date for any new unitary authority. It does not quantify the effect of reorganisation on the forecasts.
findings.matters: A forecast that does not reflect a known structural change in the council's own status is a gap that finance directors across the county area will need to address in their own plans.
findings.figures: None given in the paper for this point
findings.quote: The MTFS has not taken any account of the impact of LGR.

findings.paper_title: MTFS and Business Strategy Oct-26 FINAL
findings.headline: The paper states that Core Spending Power will fall in real terms across the transitional period and beyond.
findings.detail: The paper shows Revenue Support Grant falling from £4,281k in 2026/27 to £3,854k in 2027/28 and £3,400k in 2028/29. It also says the Fair Funding Review and business rates reset present considerable risk to grant funding.
findings.matters: A real-terms fall in Core Spending Power is the headline measure of government support that peer councils and lenders compare when assessing council funding.
findings.quote: Although some transitional arrangements were applied to limit the impact, the Council’s Core Spending Power (CSP) will fall in real terms across the transitional period and beyond.

findings.paper_title: MTFS and Business Strategy Oct-26 FINAL
findings.headline: The Nottinghamshire Business Rates Pool was dissolved at the end of 2025/26, and the councils will not pool again in 2026/27.
findings.detail: The Nottinghamshire Finance Officers Association agreed the dissolution after reviewing that the risks now outweighed any rewards following the business rates reset. The paper says the pool had retained over £74m of growth in earlier years.
findings.matters: Leaving a business rates pool removes a source of retained growth, and other councils considering the same reset will weigh the same risk against the reward.
findings.figures: Over £74m of growth retained locally by the pool in earlier years; £2.971m Baseline Funding Level for Broxtowe
findings.quote: As such, the NFOA agreed to dissolve the Nottinghamshire Business Rates Pool at the end of 2025/26 and revoke the intention to pool again in 2026/27 with MHCLG.

findings.paper_title: MTFS and Business Strategy Oct-26 FINAL
findings.headline: Broxtowe received £739k of Adjustment Support Grant in 2026/27, with no commitment to extend it into 2027/28.
findings.detail: The paper describes the grant as a one-off allocation that gave temporary protection to Core Spending Power. It records that the loss of this grant presents a real funding risk, and the MTFS assumes it ends after 2026/27.
findings.matters: A one-off grant that makes up part of a council's 2026/27 funding and is not assumed to continue is a funding cliff that other councils with similar protections will also face.
findings.figures: £739k Adjustment Support Grant in 2026/27; nil in 2027/28 onwards in the MTFS
findings.quote: This late change saw Broxtowe receive £739k in Adjustment Support Grant in 2026/27. There is currently no commitment to extend this grant into 2027/28 and beyond

findings.paper_title: MTFS and Business Strategy Oct-26 FINAL
findings.headline: Broxtowe secured £21.1m of Towns Deal funding for development projects in Stapleford and a £16.5m grant for the Kimberley Means Business regeneration project.
findings.detail: The paper says these grants have boosted the General Fund capital programme alongside the Bramcote scheme. It also notes the council is seeking further funding through the East Midlands County Combined Authority.
findings.matters: Externally funded regeneration grants reduce the council's reliance on borrowing and capital receipts, which peers and lenders will want to see in the funding mix.
findings.figures: £21.1m Towns Deal funding for Stapleford; £16.5m grant for Kimberley Means Business
findings.quote: The Council was successful in bidding for the Government’s Towns Deal funding to regenerate Stapleford, with £21.1m being secured for development projects in Stapleford.
